jobs.description:
Applied RL Engineer-Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Applied RL Engineer
Location: 100% Remote (United States)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually
Experience: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are looking for a Reinforcement Learning Engineer to design, train, and deploy RL-based systems for high-impact decision-making problems where supervised learning alone is insufficient. The role requires deep familiarity with modern reinforcement learning algorithms, simulation environments, reward modeling, and the engineering complexity of training and evaluating policies at scale. The ideal candidate has both research depth and engineering pragmatism, with experience taking RL solutions out of the lab and into production where stability, safety, and ongoing improvement are critical.

Required Qualifications
  • Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field; or equivalent applied experience.
  • Six or more years of combined RL research and engineering experience.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and modern deep learning frameworks.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one major RL library or in-house RL stack.
  • Solid understanding of probability, optimization, and the theoretical foundations of RL.
  • Experience designing and tuning reward functions in non-trivial environments.
  • Familiarity with simulation environments and large-scale experience collection.
  • Experience training neural network policies on GPU clusters.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Track record of shipping or publishing impactful RL work.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with RLHF for large language models.
  • Familiarity with multi-agent RL or hierarchical RL.
  • Exposure to robotics, control systems, or autonomous driving.
  • Publications in RL or related research venues.
  • Open-source contributions to RL libraries or environments.

Heart Failure

In Abbott’s Heart Failure (HF) business, we’re developing solutions to diagnose, monitor and manage heart failure, allowing people to restore their health and get on with their lives.

  • Strong understanding of payor and insurance reimbursement landscape.

  • Strong executive presence, clinical/technical presentations to audiences of 1–50 stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to influence cross‑functional buying groups (value analysis committees, supply chain, service line leadership) Influencing multiple key stakeholders to drive growth.
  • Strong understanding of market dynamics
  • Strong commercial acumen with ability to produce data‑driven territory strategies, forecasting models, and QBRs using CRM platforms (Salesforce preferred), analytics, and Excel.

Our rapid diagnostics solutions are helping address some of the world’s greatest healthcare challenges.

jobs.title: Inventory Manager
jobs.excerpt: Our client, a rapidly growing Amazon FBM (Fulfilled by Merchant) business sourcing a wide range of products from China, is looking for a highly analytical and detail-oriented Inventory Manager to support the companys focus on fast fulfillment, operational efficiency, and data-driven decision-making.
jobs.description:
Our client, a rapidly growing Amazon FBM (Fulfilled by Merchant) business sourcing a wide range of products from China, is looking for a highly analytical and detail-oriented Inventory Manager to support the companys focus on fast fulfillment, operational efficiency, and data-driven decision-making. In this role, they will be responsible for overseeing all inventory operations, from procurement and inbound logistics to spare parts control and returns processing. A major part of the position involves building and maintaining advanced data systems and dashboards in Google Sheets, ensuring accurate stock visibility and operational efficiency across all channels.

About the company:

The company is an e-commerce brand built around movement, energy, and family fun. Best known for its high-quality outdoor products - especially trampolines designed for safety and joy - it is growing fast across global marketplaces. The company values initiative, quality, and people who take ownership of their work. If youre passionate about e-commerce and want to play a key role in building something meaningful, you might be a great fit.

Key responsibilities:

Inventory & Stock Control

  • Maintain accurate and real-time stock levels for all SKUs across Amazon FBM channels and internal databases.
  • Develop and maintain Google Sheets dashboards to track inventory, shipments, returns, and reorder points.
  • Monitor spare parts inventory, ensuring correct allocation and timely replenishment.
  • Forecast inventory needs based on sales trends and product lifecycle data.
  • Prevent stockouts and overstock through precise data-driven planning.

Procurement & Supplier Coordination

  • Coordinate purchase orders and shipping schedules with suppliers in China.
  • Track inbound shipments and lead times using structured data sheets.
  • Follow up with suppliers and freight forwarders on delays, discrepancies, or quality issues.
  • Support cost analysis and order optimization using spreadsheet models.

Returns & Reverse Logistics

  • Manage returns and spare parts processing, including inspection, refurbishment, restocking, or disposal.
  • Update stock and status in Google Sheets and inventory systems in real time.
  • Optimize workflows for handling returned goods efficiently.

Data Analysis & Reporting

  • Build automated reports in Google Sheets with formulas, pivot tables, charts, and scripts (e.g., Apps Script or integrations).
  • Track KPIs such as stock accuracy, turnover rates, aging inventory, and reorder performance.
  • Identify inefficiencies and propose data-backed improvements.
  • Collaborate with other departments to provide clear inventory visibility and forecasts.

Process & System Optimization

  • Integrate data between Google Sheets, Amazon Seller Central, and warehouse systems.
  • Standardize inventory tracking templates and ensure all team members follow consistent data procedures.
  • Support automation initiatives to reduce manual work.

Requirements:

  • Proven experience as an Inventory Manager, Supply Chain Manager, or similar role in Amazon FBM and FBA.
  • Expert-level Google Sheets skills: Data visualization and reporting
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
  • Experience managing spare parts, returns, or similar technical products.
  • Familiarity with Amazon Seller Central and FBM workflows.
  • Experience working with Chinese suppliers and freight forwarders.
  • Excellent English communication skills.
  • Experience integrating Google Sheets with other tools (e.g., Zapier, APIs, or ERP systems).
  • Knowledge of 3PL operations and warehouse management.
  • Understanding of international shipping and import processes
  • Strong process mindset and ability to build SOPs.

What We Offer:

  • Work for a Market-proven, fast-growing company.
  • Competitive salary and bonus opportunities
  • Supportive work environment.
  • Friendly International start-up environment.
  • Self-development trainings and courses.
  • Be a part of something bigger, where you can have autonomy over your work.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About A1MA1M Solutions is a woman-owned small business driven by the aspiration to provide value to our customers, employees, partners, and community while remaining aligned to our guiding principles of foundational values, deliberate focus, and empathetic connection.
jobs.description:
About A1M

A1M Solutions is a woman-owned small business driven by the aspiration to provide value to our customers, employees, partners, and community while remaining aligned to our guiding principles of foundational values, deliberate focus, and empathetic connection.

A1M’s mission is to preserve and improve government healthcare programs that are lifelines for underserved people in the United States, including people in poverty, elderly people, members of ethnic and racial minorities, immigrants, and refugees. We look for projects with nation-wide impact at the intersection of policy, data, and user experience design.

Besides building useful and usable digital services, A1M helps teams improve their agile, user-centered design practices – or helps them get started. Our goal is not just to build sustainable public services, but also to leave our teaming partners and customers more skilled and more confident in the future.

Technology Delivery at A1M

A1M Technology Delivery Practice staff meet client and user needs by planning, building, and maintaining solutions that involve programming and scripting. Our practice includes product managers, software engineers, and data analysts. We analyze government client challenges and identify how best to help the client meet their goals, which may involve custom code, low code, and no code approaches.

Technology Delivery Practice staff work in cross-functional, cross-organizational teams with designers and policy subject matter experts. We approach challenges with flexibility, patience, thoughtful communication, and solid best practices in agile product management and development. We value high-trust teams.

About this Role

As an A1M Senior Software Engineer, you work with minimal guidance to design and implement complex, scalable systems. You collaborate with the team to break down ambiguous or complex goals into concrete, feasible steps that align with and inform wider system strategy. Senior engineers do not always have formal management or lead responsibilities, but an interest in teaching and coaching is essential.

Skills and Responsibilities

Technical capabilities

  • Build and maintain complex, scalable systems across application and/or infrastructure layers, and multiple components or services, using languages and frameworks such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Django.
  • Own components or services from development through deployment, monitoring, and production support
  • Deploy and manage systems in cloud environments, including AWS services, using CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and infrastructure as code where appropriate.
  • Design, build, and integrate APIs and data flows, working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL and cloud-based data services as needed.
  • Shape system design and contribute to architectural decisions, including writing decision documents and creating diagrams
  • Drive improvements in code quality, automated testing, linting, and development standards using appropriate tools and practices for the stack.
  • Contribute to robust DevOps practices, including deployment, monitoring, and incident response
  • Mentor engineers, review code and technical designs, and contribute to team growth and technical direction
  • Collaborate to break down ambiguous or complex goals into concrete, feasible steps
  • Seek out and share new technologies and skills that support project goals
  • Participate in discussions with internal and external stakeholders

Universal Categories for all A1M Senior Practitioners

Communication and collaboration

  • Build connections and relationships between people, teams/projects, and A1M and clients in ways that prevent and break down silos, enabling new opportunities for improved delivery.
  • Get buy-in from relevant parties (teammates, team leads, government stakeholders, etc.) to make sure necessary work happens.
  • Proactively recognize risks and conflicts within the team and clients, help identify approaches, and take action – manage up (understanding timing, context and other pressures, etc.) and escalate when appropriate.
  • Evaluate your own skills and deliverables and take action based on self-assessment. This might include proactively reaching out to other team members for help upskilling in skill gap areas.

Cross-domain understanding

  • Initiate and drive projects that require working with multiple people in other disciplines and practices on challenging problems.
  • Coach and mentor people not just within your own practice or discipline, but across practice areas – for example, designers coaching engineers.
  • Anticipate and proactively provide information needed by other practices and disciplines.

Government domain acumen

  • Proactively identify and respond to government requirements or policy that may impact project work, such as accessibility, PRA, FOIA, acquisition regulations, and security compliance.
  • Sufficient government understanding to anticipate needs of government partners and users, and be prepared to speak to them proactively.
  • Trusted to represent the company and team to clients, including in challenging situations.

Qualifications

8 years of relevant professional experience.

Your resume or portfolio should demonstrate:

  • Ability to write high-quality, tested, maintainable, and reusable code in production software systems
  • Advanced proficiency in one or more modern programming languages, with professional experience in technologies relevant to our stack, such as TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, or Go
  • Expertise in how to build secure, compliant software and minimize risk of vulnerabilities
  • Expertise in one or more adjacent specializations, such as data engineering, DevOps, cloud infrastructure, or application security, and the ability to flex skills as needed
  • Capable of operating as a self-starter in ambiguous environments, identifying high-impact work independently and executing on it
  • Proven ability to communicate technical results clearly and effectively to diverse stakeholders
  • Experience working in government consulting engagements

Preferred:

  • Experience building or maintaining production applications using technologies such as Django, PostgreSQL, or AWS services.
  • Experience working with a social impact-focused product team or in civic tech
  • Experience working with distributed, cross-functional teams, including product managers, designers, engineers, and subject matter experts
  • Personal experience with government health and human services programs
  • Working knowledge of Medicare, the ACA, MACRA, Medicaid, or CHIP
  • Familiarity with SAFe and agile methodologies
  • Experience integrating modern applications with existing systems, APIs, or legacy platforms
  • Experience working on large-scale applications and systems

Applicant Requirements

  • Our contracts require employees to work from the United States. That includes all 50 US states, the District of Columbia, and all US territories.
  • A1M employees must have been residents in the United States for 3 of the past 5 years.
  • Due to tax reasons, A1M employees cannot reside in New York state.
  • You must already have legal authorization to work within the US and not require ongoing visa sponsorship to maintain legal authorization to work.
  • You must be a permanent US resident.
  • Because A1M employees have access to government data and systems, new hires will need to complete a Public Trust form. Public Trust is a type of background investigation, but it is not a security clearance. Depending on the role, you must complete either the Standard Form 85 (SF85) or 85P (SF85P) questionnaire. You will at the very least get asked questions about where you’ve lived, worked, went to school, military history, police records, and substance use. You’ll also need to have your fingerprints taken.
  • Our partners primarily work on Eastern Standard Time (EST), and will require flexibility in your hours if you reside outside of EST. We do offer flexibility for non-work-related life responsibilities during the day.
  • Active participation in client virtual meetings, including being on camera, is an essential function that helps strengthen trust and open communication. Employees who are unable to meet this expectation due to a disability, medical condition, religious practice, or other protected reason may request reasonable accommodations by contacting People Operations.

Compensation and benefits

This is a fully remote full-time, permanent position. The salary range for this role is $125,000 – $155,000. This range is set by our contracts and reflects the full range for someone in this position over time, so you may not start at the top of the range.

A1M offers a benefits package that includes:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Life insurance, short-term disability, and optional voluntary benefits
  • 401(k) retirement benefits with employer matching
  • Four weeks of paid time off, seven company holidays, two personal days, and your birthday off
  • Paid volunteer time
  • Wellness reimbursements
  • Budgets to support training, development, travel, and office supply needs
  • Donations to a nonprofit of your choice upon hire and a few times throughout each year

Interview process

We typically have five rounds of conversations to help ensure every employee we hire is the right addition for us and that we’re the right fit for them. Each interview is about 45–60 minutes long.

  1. A1M Overview - We like to start off by getting to know more about you, how you work, what you are looking for in your next role, and what you’re passionate about. This is your opportunity to ask questions and get a feel for us as A1M. We’ll talk about our mission and vision, and what we hope to accomplish through the business. We’ll also cover some particulars about federal contracting that may affect the timelines of when folks can expect to start. We talk about the type of contracts we have, and how our team tends to work.
  2. Technical Assessment - If our work at A1M broadly matches what you’re looking for, we’ll set up time to get into the nitty-gritty of your technical skills. In this conversation, you’ll meet with one of our managers to walk through one or two projects in-depth that you feel are most relevant to A1M’s work so that we can get an in-depth understanding of your skill set and interests. Please be prepared to speak about one or two projects you feel are most relevant to the work of A1M.
  3. Values Interview - After the technical assessment, we’ll schedule a conversation focused on A1M’s core values. This interview helps us understand how you approach your work, collaborate with others, and align with the way we operate as an organization, including areas like impact, collaboration, relationship management, curiosity, and active listening.
  4. Project Overview - Based on what we’ve learned in our prior conversations, we will match your unique background and goals with the right opportunity. Members of the project team will share the day-to-day of the project to outline its vision, objectives, and team dynamics. This conversation ensures the specific position aligns with your career goals as well as ensuring you’ll be successful on the team.
  5. Offer - At this point, you’ve made it! You'll meet with our leadership to go over the offer letter and have a chance to ask any remaining questions.

Equal Employment Opportunity

A1M Solutions is building a culturally diverse and pluralistic organization committed to working in a multicultural environment where differences are valued and respected. Women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities, members of ethnic minorities, foreign-born residents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.

A1M Solutions is an equal-opportunity employer. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

As a federal contractor and subcontractor, we certify that we do not operate any programs promoting DEI that violate any applicable Federal anti-discrimination laws.

About the role

Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. You work through AI agents daily, doing the work of a bigger team.

What you will do

Salesforce and GTM stack

Revenue analytics and data model

AI and automation

Ownership

jobs.excerpt: Nexla, brieflyNexla is the data connectivity layer for enterprise AI.
jobs.description:
Nexla, briefly

Nexla is the data connectivity layer for enterprise AI. Over 1,000 bidirectional connectors give agents real-time access to data and actions over MCP. Nexla's Agentic Data Integration handles high-volume streaming ETL, CDC, and Document ETL. At the core of the platform is Helix, a context engine that continuously learns from metadata, schemas, telemetry, and documentation to give agents accurate context and keep pipelines reliable. Nexla processes over a trillion records a month for enterprises including DoorDash, LiveRamp, LinkedIn, and J&J. Honorable Mention in the Gartner Magic Quadrant™ for Data Integration Tools, and top-rated by customers on Gartner Peer Insights four years running.

About the role

You’ll own the technical relationship with our accounts: onboarding, implementation, adoption, escalations, and everything that happens when a pipeline that used to work stops working.

You are the person the customer's data team calls, and the person who tells them the truth when the answer is inconvenient. Most of the job is conversation: understanding what they are actually trying to do, explaining what the platform will and will not do for them, keeping their expectations aligned with reality, and raising problems while they are still small.

The technical part matters, but not in the way people usually assume. We want a generalist who has built things before and therefore understands how the pieces fit together: what a Kubernetes cluster is for, why a VPN tunnel might be the bottleneck, what a stack trace is telling you, what a slow query looks like. You will not be asked to be the deepest engineer in the room. You will be asked to be the person who can talk to the deepest engineer in the room, understand them, and translate what they said to a VP who has thirty seconds.

What you will do

  • Own the technical relationship for a portfolio of accounts. You are the continuity: the person who knows their environment, their history, and their constraints.
  • Lead onboarding and implementation. Understand what the customer is trying to build, design the integration with them, and guide it to production.
  • Run the hard conversations. A missed date, a degraded pipeline, a limitation they did not expect, a customer who is upset and technically wrong. You stay calm, keep credibility, and land on a next step everyone agrees to.
  • Flag risk early and in writing. Adoption stalling, a champion who left, a project quietly losing sponsorship, an architecture heading somewhere that will not scale. Flagging a risk three weeks early is worth more here than fixing it heroically after it lands.
  • Translate between audiences. The same situation explained to a data engineer, to a security reviewer, and to a VP, without losing any of them.
  • Troubleshoot alongside the customer: failed runs, schema drift, connector and authentication failures, connectivity problems, performance issues. You do the first-line diagnosis and bring engineering a clear reproduction when it needs to escalate.
  • Partner with CSM and Support on renewal risk, and hand expansion signals to Sales.
  • Mentor other SAs on how to handle customers, not just how to solve problems.

What you need

Communication and customer ownership (the core of the role)

  • You can explain a technical concept to a non-technical stakeholder without either dumbing it down or losing them.
  • You handle conflict without escalating it. You can tell a customer no, or "that was our mistake" and keep the relationship intact.
  • You build trust over months, not meetings. Customers should ask for you by name.
  • You write clearly and unprompted: summaries, next steps, and owners after every meaningful call.
  • You raise problems early, including your own. We would much rather hear "this is slipping and here is why" than a confident status update that turns out to be wrong.
  • You push back on bad requirements instead of silently building them.

Technical breadth

You should be a generalist who has built software or data systems at some point. Not necessarily an expert in any one of these, but genuinely conversant in most of them, in the way someone is conversant after having actually worked with them:

  • Python. You can read someone else's script, follow what it does, make a modification, and understand stack traces.
  • SQL. Comfortable writing joins, aggregations, and filters. You can look at a slow query and have a sensible first guess about why.
  • Data pipelines and integration. APIs and their common failure modes (rate limits, pagination, retries, auth expiry), webhooks, CDC, file-based ingestion, batch versus streaming trade-offs.
  • Cloud data platforms. Working familiarity with at least one of Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, or a major cloud data warehouse.
  • Authentication. You understand what OAuth, SSO, service accounts, and API keys are and roughly how they work. You can follow a conversation about a failing token exchange.
  • Networking. DNS, firewalls, private connectivity, VPNs and SSH tunnels. You do not need to configure them, but you need to understand the concepts well enough to hold a productive call with a customer's network team and know when the network is the problem rather than the platform.
  • Containers and Kubernetes. Conceptual understanding only: what a container is, what Kubernetes does, why workloads run in pods, what it means when something runs out of memory. You will not be administering clusters.
  • Linux. Comfortable enough in a terminal to read a log file, check a process, or run a curl command.

Experience

  • 5+ years in technical customer-facing work: solutions architecture, implementation, technical account management, professional services, consulting, support engineering, or a data engineering role that involved heavy stakeholder contact.
  • At least some of that spent hands-on building, not only advising.
  • Experience owning accounts or projects through delivery, not just handing off.

Nice to have

  • Prior experience at a data integration, ETL, or data platform vendor.
  • Background in data engineering or software engineering earlier in your career.
  • Experience in a regulated industry (healthcare, financial services, insurance).
  • Entrepreneurial experience or similar (having worked at a fast-paced startup environment).

What this role is not

  • Not a support queue. You own outcomes on named accounts.
  • Not a deep engineering role.
  • Not a pure relationship role either. You need to be technical enough to earn the customer's respect in the first meeting.

Interview process

  1. Recruiter screen (30 min)
  2. Hiring manager conversation (45 min)
  3. Technical breadth session (60 min): troubleshooting reasoning, plus basic Python and SQL
  4. Customer scenario (60 min): you handle a difficult account situation with a panel playing customer roles

Why Nexla? Why now?

A few large companies - DoorDash, SentinelOne, Johnson & Johnson, LinkedIn, Amex, Integrity Marketing, among them use Nexla for data integration. Connectors, runtime, transformations, scheduling, the parts of the stack where data has to move between systems reliably.

The reason this is an interesting moment to join is what the agent shift is doing to the category. Data integration used to mean "land this data in that warehouse so a human can look at it." That product is mature. What it's becoming is closer to "an agent asks a business question, and the platform figures out which data and what code and which APIs add up to a real answer." That's a much bigger problem, and most of the architecture for it hasn't been built yet by anyone.

A concrete example. A revenue team wants to ask "which enterprise customers are showing renewal risk" and get a real answer through whatever agent or app they work in. Today there is no clean way to answer that question, it requires CRM, usage, support, and billing data joined in org-specific ways, and the calling agent can't just invoke a tool that returns the right answer unless someone first establishes whether the underlying data is even capable of producing one.

That is the system we are building. A probe agent investigates the data plane whether the right fields are populated, whether freshness is adequate, whether the joins exist, whether credentials cover the required scope and returns a grounded feasibility answer. Where there are gaps, Express.dev composes the pipelines to close them. The capability is then exposed as an MCP server: "renewal risk" as a curated product, with the business logic correct and the query semantics described well enough that the calling agent uses it as intended. The MCP Gateway governs which agents can call which capabilities, with the policies, audit, and observability an enterprise control plane requires.

The bet is that ten years of connector work, an enterprise customer base, and a runtime that already moves real volume are the right foundation to define this layer from.

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. Why You’ll Love This Role

At Cribl, we're transforming from a flagship-product company into a multi-product powerhouse - and every non-routine business event, whether an acquisition, a product launch, or a go-to-market shift, adds complexity our data, definitions, and reporting weren't built to handle. As the Analytics Business Partner, you're the person who closes that gap - translating a new product or customer into our existing data, systems and reporting: how it connects to what we already have, how value is attributed, how we define and track it going forward. Reporting to the VP of Data & Analytics — part of Cribl's broader Business Operations organization alongside Strategy & Operations and Business Effectiveness — you'll operate horizontally across the business rather than embedding in a single function.

This is a high-impact role for a strategist who thrives on ambiguity and builds order from chaos. If you are eager to contribute to a company poised for generational success, we want to hear from you.


As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

  • Diagnose and Drive the Solution. When a non-routine business event doesn't fit with how we currently track or report on the business, define the solution. Whether a system change, a new process or policy, or a different data model, serve as the Directly Responsible Individual (DRI) for working with the necessary x-functional teams to get it delivered
  • M&A Integration. When we acquire a company, own and drive how its products and customers fit into our existing reporting and data models, ensuring we can capture the impact of the acquisition post deal close
  • New Product Launch. When we launch a new product, understand how Product defines its success metrics, and make sure our models, definitions, and reporting can track against those metrics post launch

When a change spans across the Data and Analytics team (Data Engineering, Analytics, Data Science, Data Governance), sequence who does what first, own the handoffs between them, catch duplication or gaps before they cost the team time, and push the pace when the event demands it
  • Stand Up the Business Intelligence Council. Maintain a working picture of how GTM, Finance, Product, and other functions operate, knowing who to engage so a project doesn’t start or drift, without the right people engaged.   • We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones – you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours

If You've Got It - We Want It

  • Fluency across GTM, Finance, Product, and other functions - enough to know that 'customer' may mean something different to Sales than it does to Finance, and to reconcile the difference rather than pick a side
  • You can join multiple tables, write a CTE, and get the aggregation grain right - enough to answer your own question - though hands-on query and dashboard work won't be your primary responsibility in this role
  • Given a reporting issue, you know not to default to a “data-only” answer - you can tell whether the real problem is a system that isn't capturing the right data, a process nobody owns, or a data model that no longer matches the business
  • Ability to flex your communication style as needed - equally fluent giving execs the top-line takeaway and working through the nuances with the operational teams to drive a solution
  • First hand experience ensuring a business’s data and reporting keep up following an acquisition or new product launch - designing and driving the solution so the business doesn’t lose visibility into itself
  • Bonus: experience inside a post-close M&A integration, a new product introduction, or a go-to-market model change
  • Bonus: experience in late-stage B2B SaaS startups (i.e., Series E+) and / or early public B2B SaaS companies (e.g., 3-5k employees)

In addition to a competitive salary, Cribl also offers a generous benefits package which includes health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and paid time off, a fertility treatment benefit, 401(k), and equity.

Base Salary Range
$190,000—$255,000 USD

Bring Your Whole Self

jobs.excerpt: As a UI/UX Researcher & Designer at Intelerad, you will play a meaningful role in shaping how clinicians and healthcare professionals interact with our medical imaging products.
jobs.description:
As a UI/UX Researcher & Designer at Intelerad, you will play a meaningful role in shaping how clinicians and healthcare professionals interact with our medical imaging products. You will independently own research and design for one or more product areas, partnering with product managers, developers, and end users to turn complex clinical needs and business goals into intuitive, high-quality experiences, from early discovery through to successful release. You will bring a balanced skillset, grounding design decisions in rigorous user research, translating insight into compelling, usable interfaces, and helping raise the quality of UX practice across the team.

Key Responsibilities

Research

  • Independently plan and lead qualitative and quantitative UX research across the product lifecycle, using field studies, direct observation, interviews, workflow and task analysis, usability testing, and surveys to identify opportunities, validate assumptions, and shape product direction.

  • Set research priorities and methodologies for your product area in partnership with product management; recruit participants and moderate sessions with clinicians and other end users.

  • Synthesize research data into personas, journey maps, and actionable insights, and translate findings into design and product recommendations that influence roadmap decisions.

  • Own and evolve our research repository so findings stay discoverable and continue to inform current and future work.

Design

  • Lead the design of intuitive interfaces from concept to release, grounded in a strong understanding of user goals, clinical workflows, and product requirements, delivering screen layouts, interaction patterns, and UI elements that meet usability and business standards.

  • Own design work end-to-end: produce wireframes, storyboards, functional prototypes, and detailed specifications that clearly communicate intent to developers, QA, and technical writers.

  • Drive the creation and adoption of design standards that ensure consistency across the product suite, and guide developers through UI design decisions and trade-offs during implementation.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Build trust with users through deep empathy, active listening, and strong facilitation, enabling a thorough understanding of their goals, workflows, and challenges.

  • Present design and research findings clearly to audiences ranging from engineers to product leadership, and lead design and research critique sessions to ensure alignment and quality.

  • Mentor and provide feedback to less experienced designers and researchers, sharing methods and best practices across the team.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), User Experience (UX) Design, Interaction Design, Human Factors / Ergonomics, Psychology, Graphic Design, or equivalent experience.

  • 4+ years of experience in UI/UX design and UX research, with a portfolio demonstrating both strong web and mobile design capabilities and end-to-end research work.

  • Proficiency in industry-standard design tools, including Figma and/or Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Illustrator, XD, or equivalent).

  • Demonstrated expertise in wireframing, prototyping, and producing design specifications.

  • Demonstrated experience independently planning and leading user research using qualitative and quantitative methods, and synthesizing findings into personas, journey maps, and actionable insights.

  • Familiarity with UX research tools and repositories (e.g., Dovetail, UserZoom, Optimal Workshop, or similar).

  • Strong knowledge of HCI principles and design best practices.

  • Proven ability to communicate design rationale and research findings effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior stakeholders.

  • Excellent spoken and written English, or equivalent.

Preferred Qualifications & Special Requirements

  • Experience prototyping with HTML and CSS or similar front-end tools.

  • Experience in healthcare IT or complex enterprise software; experience conducting research with clinical or healthcare users.

  • Familiarity with accessibility standards (WCAG) and inclusive design practices.

  • Familiarity with survey design and basic statistical analysis.

  • Experience working in Agile development environments.

About the Role

The Oncology Trial Navigator will play a critical role in connecting Signatera patients to life-changing clinical trial opportunities. As a front-line clinical expert, you will be responsible for the end-to-end execution of patient matching workflows—from initial AI-enabled screening to successful enrollment at a clinical trial site.

You will serve as the primary clinical point of contact for external stakeholders, including treating oncologists, principal investigators (PIs), and research coordinators. This role combines deep oncology clinical knowledge with high-touch stakeholder engagement in a fast-scaling, mission-driven environment. You will work closely with the Senior Manager of Oncology Trial Navigation to pilot and refine the navigation service, providing the "on-the-ground" insights necessary to scale this function across the oncology domain.

What You’ll Do

Physician & Site Engagement

  • Conduct high-volume, structured outreach to oncologists, PIs, and research coordinators regarding trial-eligible patients identified through Natera’s platforms.
  • Act as a clinical consultant to research sites, delivering patient eligibility notifications and facilitating seamless referral workflows.
  • Track patient progression from initial identification through referral and enrollment, ensuring timely follow-up and resolution of site-level bottlenecks.

Trial Matching & Medical Review

  • Operationalize outputs from Natera’s AI-enabled trial matching platform to manage a daily priority queue of potential matches.
  • Perform rigorous clinical reviews, reconciling patient molecular data (e.g., MRD status, biomarkers) and exome results with trial-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria.
  • Collaborate with the Clinical Product team to provide real-time feedback on matching accuracy, helping to refine AI algorithms and data filters.

Patient & Caregiver Support (as applicable)

  • Provide high-level, empathetic, and compliant education to patients regarding specific clinical trial opportunities and the clinical significance of their molecular results.
  • Coordinate warm handoffs to site research teams, ensuring patients feel supported and informed throughout the referral process.

Operational Excellence

  • Maintain meticulous documentation of all outreach and referral activities within CRM and tracking tools.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Participate in cross-functional collaboration with internal partners to optimize the field.

Qualifications

  • Current, active licensure as a Registered Nurse (RN), Certified Genetic Counselor (CGC), Nurse Practitioner (NP), or Physician Assistant (PA).
    • Must maintain licensure in good standing throughout employment.
    • Board Certification (e.g., OCN, CCRC, or similar) is highly preferred.
  • A master’s degree in a clinical or scientific field is preferred.

Professional Experience:

  • 3–5 years of oncology clinical experience, with at least 2 years specifically in oncology clinical research (e.g., as a Research Nurse, Coordinator, or Navigator).

  • Data Literacy: Comfort navigating large clinical datasets and translating patient records into structured eligibility requirements.
  • Systems Advocacy: Proactive in identifying workflow inefficiencies and suggesting technological or process-based solutions.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.
  • High degree of empathy and professionalism in patient-facing interactions.
  • Strong organizational skills and follow through discipline.
  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish preferred.

jobs.excerpt: Why Work at Mercer Advisors? For more than 40 years, Mercer Advisors has been helping families amplify and simplify their financial lives by integrating financial planning, investment management, business management, tax, estate, insurance, and more, all managed by a single team.
jobs.description:
Why Work at Mercer Advisors?

For more than 40 years, Mercer Advisors has been helping families amplify and simplify their financial lives by integrating financial planning, investment management, business management, tax, estate, insurance, and more, all managed by a single team. We deliver the kind of comprehensive care once reserved for only the wealthiest households.

Today, we serve over 42,800+ families across 110+ cities across the U.S. Ranked the #1 RIA Firm in the nation by Barron’s for two consecutive years, Mercer Advisors is an independent fiduciary legally bound to act in our clients’ best interests — always.*

Mercer Advisors offers a workplace that stands apart in the financial industry. More than half of our employees and client-facing professionals are women, reflecting the clients we serve. With a flexible, national footprint, we build our teams around exceptional talent — wherever they are.

Join us and help families amplify and simplify their financial lives with confidence.

* Mercer Advisors was ranked #1 for RIA firms with up to $70 billion in assets. The Barron’s top RIA ranking is based on a combination of metrics – including size, growth, service quality, technology, succession planning and others. No fee was paid for participation in the ranking, however, Mercer Advisors has paid a fee to Barron’s to use the ranking in marketing. Please see important information about the ranking criteria methodology here.

Job Summary

We're rebuilding how the Platform organization operates at Mercer Advisors — and we need someone who makes sure that transformation actually lands. This is not a coordinator role. This is not a status-tracker. This is the operating nerve center of a modern Platform org, and you'll own the systems, cadences, and discipline that determine whether we ship the right things, in the right order, at the right speed.

This role owns four things at a high level: roadmap planning and management; the end-to-end development process from intake through delivery; execution across the Platform org; and a set of shared platform utilities — including budget and resource tracking, platform metrics, vendor coordination, and serving as the primary conduit between the Platform org and central functions like compliance, legal, finance, and BI.

You'll work directly with and on behalf of the Chief Platform Officer. You give leadership clear visibility into what's on track, what's at risk, and what needs a decision. You raise unblockers before they become blockers. You carry real authority across engineering, product, and data to define how work gets done and hold the org to it. When people ask what the Platform org committed to this quarter and how we're doing against it — your answer will be the answer.

Essential Job Functions

1) Roadmap Planning and Management

  • Own and facilitate the quarterly and annual roadmap planning process — connecting business goals to squad capacity to committed delivery. Keep the rhythm consistent and the process honest: no sandbagging, no last-minute pivots that weren't surfaced early.
  • Prepare and deliver Advisors Leadership Forum (ALF) updates on behalf of the Platform org. These should be clear, well-framed, and ready — no deck that takes three hours to produce, no spin. Platform leadership should be able to walk in with confidence in what's being presented.
  • Organize and run sprint demos that are worth attending: tight, outcomes-focused, and useful to leadership. Run retrospectives that actually change behavior — not sessions that produce a parking lot and no follow-through. Own the connection between what we planned, what we shipped, and what we learned.

2) Development Process

  • Design and own the end-to-end development process — from intake and requirements through build and delivery. This is the agile operating model for the Platform org: how requests are evaluated, how work is sized and scoped, how it moves through the system, and how changes to scope get approved. These aren't suggestions — they're the standard.
  • Build and run the intake framework that scores every feature request, initiative, and technical investment against business impact, strategic alignment, squad capacity, and level of effort. Make intake legible and trusted: business stakeholders know how to submit and what happens next; squads know what's coming and why it was prioritized; nothing slides sideways into the roadmap.
  • Define roles and responsibilities across product management, engineering, design, and data — so there's no ambiguity about who decides what at each stage. Introduce estimation discipline without bureaucracy. Partner with product managers to pressure-test scoping, surface hidden dependencies, and catch scope creep before it derails a commitment.

3) Platform Utilities

  • Budget and resource allocation. Own the tracking and reporting of development hours and team capacity across the Platform org. Partner with finance to maintain budget visibility, flag variances, and support resource planning decisions. The squads do the work — this function makes sure leadership has an accurate, real-time picture of where time and money are going.
  • Platform metrics. Own the internal health metrics for the Platform org: delivery velocity, planning accuracy, intake cycle times, and system-level indicators like uptime and SLAs where they fall within scope. Partner with the appropriate teams — including customer experience and advisor experience functions — to define where platform metrics end and client-facing metrics begin, and make sure there's no gap between the two.
  • Central functions conduit. Act as the primary interface between the Platform org and central functions — compliance, legal, finance, BI, and people — that receive requests from across the organization and struggle to independently prioritize them. This role doesn't change where accountability lives (squads own their work), but it adds a prioritization lens so central teams can sequence Platform requests coherently and Platform teams aren't competing against themselves for shared capacity.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • 8+ years in PMO leadership or a senior operational role inside a product and/or technology organization — ideally at a company going through transformation, not just steady-state execution
  • Proven track record of building operating models from the ground up — not inheriting and maintaining someone else's system
  • Deep fluency in agile product delivery: how software gets built, how roadmaps get set, and what breaks when process is absent
  • Experience designing and running intake and prioritization frameworks that stakeholders actually trust and use — you've built the scoring model, defended it, and evolved it
  • Skilled at running planning cadences that work: quarterly roadmaps, sprint demos, retrospectives, and executive-facing updates that are worth the calendar time
  • Strong command of sizing and estimation methodologies — you can calibrate effort across teams without turning it into a bureaucratic ritual
  • Skilled facilitator and decision-driver — you can run a room of PMs and engineers and walk out with a decision, not a list of follow-up items
  • Proactive escalator — you surface blockers with context and a recommended path forward, not just a flag. You know when to solve it yourself and when to bring it to leadership
  • Comfortable owning budget tracking and resource allocation — you can partner with finance to maintain visibility and flag variances without needing someone to hand you a template
  • Experience coordinating across central functions — you know how to be a useful interface without becoming a bottleneck
  • Experience building executive-facing reporting that's honest, concise, and actionable — you've presented to senior leadership and know what they actually need to see
  • Data fluency — you can define metrics, read dashboards, and make decisions from them. You don't need a data team to produce your own analysis
  • Strong communicator across technical and non-technical audiences — engineers respect your understanding of the craft; business leaders trust your judgment on what the org can actually do
  • Strong cross-functional relationship builder — you can work effectively across organizational boundaries without positional authority, and you know that trust is earned over time, not assumed
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and competing priorities — you create structure where there wasn't any without needing someone to hand it to you
  • Experience in financial services or regulated industries a plus, not a requirement

Work Schedule

This professional role requires availability during standard business hours, Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM. At times, the role may have early or late hours to meet business tasks and deadlines for external and internal client needs.

Working Conditions

This position may be in a professional office environment or a dedicated home office workspace that is free of interruptions. Whether in a dedicated office or home office, basic technology needs will be provided to satisfy position requirements. Routinely sitting and standing for periods of time. No heavy lifting over 10 lbs.

We encourage all interested candidates to apply as early as possible. If a final decision has not been made by the initial deadline, subsequent applications will be reviewed as they are received.

About Dreem Health, by Sunrise

Dreem Health is America’s leading digital sleep clinic. Powered by Sunrise’s technology, Dreem Health makes sleep care simple — replacing long waits and in-lab sleep studies with home-based testing, expert telehealth visits, and personalized treatment plans that are easy for patients to follow. We’re fixing the broken sleep care journey and helping more people get the care they need — from home, on their schedule.

Dreem Health is America's leading digital sleep clinic that's fixing the broken sleep care patient journey. We connect patients with sleep specialists through a straightforward telehealth platform, eliminating lengthy wait times and complicated in-lab testing. Our clinicians diagnose sleep disorders using home-based tests and deliver effective treatment plans that patients can easily follow.

Dreem Health is managed by the Sunrise Group, a breakthrough technology company that's revolutionizing sleep care with innovative diagnostic and treatment technologies, including a home sleep test that's changing how sleep apnea is diagnosed. Together, we're tackling one of healthcare's biggest challenges: helping the 1+ billion people affected by sleep disorders get the care they deserve. Backed by Amazon's Alexa Fund and $35M in funding, we're just getting started.

Your opportunity

As a Patient Care Coordinator at Dreem Health, you’ll play a critical role in shaping the patient experience from start to finish. Max Retail is a cutting-edge technology platform enabling independent retailers and brands to sell their excess inventory online effortlessly. Our mission is to become the largest supply chain that holds no inventory, providing a seamless connection between supply and global demand. We empower our partners with the tools they need to thrive in an increasingly competitive market.

MaxRetail is a two-sided marketplace that helps independent retailers turn overstock inventory into revenue. We are hiring a Director of Sales to own the retailer acquisition engine: keep our current motion running, hit closing and conversion targets, and scale the team, playbooks and automation behind it.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will coach reps on calls, run role plays, staff tradeshow booths, and own the forecast. You will also partner with RevOps and Product to automate what can be automated and remove the bottlenecks that slow new retailer growth.

MaxRetail is moving from a sales led to a product led growth model. You will lead that shift for the sales team: keep closing today while building the self-serve paths, automation and handoffs that let the product acquire and convert more retailers on its own. Your team's focus will move toward the deals and moments where a human adds the most value.

What You'll Do:

Revenue and closing

  • Keep the current sales motion running without disruption while you improve it.

  • Drive strong, consistent close rates on our current motion.

  • Improve SQL to close conversion across inbound and outbound.

  • Own sales metrics, reporting and forecasting, with a forecast leadership can plan against.

  • Know the key business inputs that drive sales (lead volume, lead source mix, speed to lead, demo held rate, onboarding completion) and actively influence them.

Outbound team performance

  • Manage outbound SDRs to consistent, high-quality demo volume.

  • Manage full cycle closers to clear demo and closing goals.

  • Hold in-house and outsourced outbound partners to the same performance standards.

Coaching and enablement

  • Review call recordings with RevOps and turn findings into better workflows and follow up templates.

  • Run regular role plays on objection handling based on the sales playbook.

  • Join live calls with reps to help close deals and model what good looks like.

  • Scale our playbooks so new reps ramp faster and results do not depend on a few top performers.

  • Recruit, hire and train new cohorts and get them producing quickly.

Incentives and motivation

  • Design spiff and incentive plans that align with business goals and stay within budget.

  • Motivate the team to hit or exceed goals.

  • Build a supportive, uplifting, growth mindset culture where reps want to stay and improve.

Automation and scale

  • Automate cold outbound and inbound motions where it improves speed or consistency.

  • Use AI to increase team efficiency and throughput.

  • Partner with Product and RevOps to remove self serve bottlenecks and scale new seller counts.

  • Identify gaps in seller onboarding that cause new seller churn and drive the fixes.

Tradeshows

  • Own tradeshow execution end to end: activation, staffing and the onsite experience.

  • Ensure the team collects leads and gives demos on site.

  • Own conversion of tradeshow leads after the show.

First 90 days

  1. Days 1 to 30: learn the motion, sit in on calls, audit the pipeline, metrics and current playbook.

  2. Days 31 to 60: launch a weekly call review and role play cadence, propose a spiff plan, and present a forecast.

  3. Days 61 to 90: ship the first automation or AI workflow, name the top onboarding gaps behind new seller churn, and set a hiring plan for the next cohort.

Required

  • 10+ years in sales, including 3+ years in sales management, managing a team of SDRs and closers to quota.

  • Proven record at a technology company, ideally one that grew from startup to scale while you were there.

  • Experience building and managing a remote sales team and the culture that keeps it accountable and connected

  • Owned the implementation of an AI or automation tool for a sales team, including process redesign, training, and driving adoption until it became part of the daily workflow.

  • A proven closer who can jump on live calls with reps and close the deal, building the team's trust by leading from the front.

  • A record of hitting conversion and activity targets in a high volume, transactional or SMB motion.

  • Experience designing compensation, spiff or incentive plans within a budget.

  • Strong forecasting and reporting skills; comfortable working in HubSpot or a similar CRM.

  • Experience hiring and ramping new reps in cohorts on a short timeline.

  • A coaching style built on call review and role play.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling to independent retailers or in a marketplace business.

  • Experience managing outsourced outbound or lead gen partners.

  • Tradeshow sales experience, from booth staffing to post-show follow up.

We want a leader who raises the bar and lifts people up at the same time.

Capacity Planning & Forecasting

Operational Execution & Deployment

  • Oversee day-to-day workforce allocation, ensuring field teams, sub-contractors, and technical specialists are fully vetted, badged, compliant, and deployed on schedule across customer sites.

Performance & Operational Reporting

Cross-Functional Alignment

jobs.title: Product Designer (US - Part-time, Contract)
jobs.excerpt: Spate is a trend intelligence platform for consumer brands in beauty, wellness, and food and beverage.
jobs.description:
Spate is a trend intelligence platform for consumer brands in beauty, wellness, and food and beverage. We analyze anonymous, aggregated public consumer data to spot emerging trends early and explain why they're growing, so brands can make product and marketing decisions with confidence.

Our founders, Yarden Horwitz and Olivier Zimmer, started Google's Trendspotting division and called trends like turmeric, cold brew, and face masks before they went mainstream. Spate is Y Combinator-backed, and more than 200 brands use it, including Sephora, L'Oréal Paris, Estée Lauder Companies, Unilever, P&G, and e.l.f. Our data regularly appears in The New York Times, WWD, British Vogue, and The Business of Fashion.

About the role

We're looking for a part-time contract product designer to shape Spate's core product: the dashboard where brand teams explore trends, build reports, and work with our AI assistant.

Our platform will change a lot over the next year or two as we rebuild around LLM-powered features. We already ship an AI Assistant, AI Reports (an LLM powered dashboard builder), and in-dashboard summaries and analysis. We need someone who can work out what those experiences should be, not just how they should look.

Our users are brand innovation teams, product marketers, social media teams, and agencies. Most aren't data analysts, so much of the job is turning dense trend data into something clear and actionable.

You'll join the Frontend & UX team, four people including you, and work closely with our frontend lead. The role is fully remote and part-time, about 20 hours a week. You’ll need to be based in US Central Time (UTC−6) or US Eastern Time (UTC-5). We require you to be available for core collaboration hours of 9:00 AM–12:00 PM Eastern.

This is a remote, Part-time contractor position.

What you'll own

The product, not just the screens. At Spate, product design and UI/UX design happen together. Features aren't fully defined and then handed to a designer. You'll help decide what we build and why, and stay involved from the first conversation to launch. You'll work with our frontend lead to choose the right deliverable for each problem: a written proposal, a user flow, a prototype, or a full Figma spec.

Finding problems worth solving. Find user pain points on your own, through customer calls, feedback, and usage data. Then take them from problem to proposal: frame the problem, explore options, and make the case for a direction. Leadership sets the overall direction and can help point you at problems, but you won't need our input to get started.

How our AI features work. Decide when something should be a chat, a report, or an inline summary. Define how we show where an insight came from, and how we handle loading, uncertainty, and wrong answers. Help shape the voice and structure of AI-generated insights, because in an LLM product the words are part of the UX.

The design system. We have a Figma library and a React component library that are only loosely in sync. You'll own the system's principles and the Figma side, and partner with our frontend engineers to make the two a single source of truth. The goal is that everyday design decisions are answered by the system, so engineers can ship UI that feels like Spate without waiting on design.

AI quality, over time. As the role settles in, you'll help define what a good AI answer looks like for our users, and contribute to how we review user feedback and evaluate our LLM features.

Requirements

What we're looking for

We care more about mindset than years of experience. You're driven, you care about making a good product, and you have a growth mindset. You value autonomy and self-direction.

  • 2+ years of product design experience, with work shipped in a real product.
  • Strong product opinions. You think about what to build and why, not just how it looks, and you're comfortable defending and revising your ideas.
  • A portfolio that shows how you framed problems, not just how you solved them. At least one case study should start from a fuzzy problem with no spec.
  • Experience with, or a strong interest in, data-heavy products such as dashboards, analytics, or reporting tools.
  • You've worked within or contributed to a design system, and understand how components and patterns scale.
  • Real curiosity about AI products, ideally with some hands-on exploration.
  • Strong written communication. We're remote and you're part-time, so your proposals and decisions need to stand on their own.

  • Familiarity with consumer goods, beauty, food, or marketing and insights tools.
  • Comfort building quick functional prototypes with AI tools to test ideas against real outputs.

Your first 90 days

  1. At 20 hours a week, we'll keep the first three months focused.
  2. First 30 days: Learn the product and the people who use it. Watch a few customer calls, review feedback and usage data, and ship your first improvements to the user experience.
  3. By day 60: Design your first feature solving a major user pain point or goal.
  4. By day 90: Work with the rest of the team to ship your feature into production.

How we work

Contributors at Spate work flexibly, with few meetings, a lot of impact, and real say over the direction of their work. Leadership sets product direction and priorities, and you shape how we get there. That means bringing proposals rather than waiting for briefs.

Our aesthetic is cool, smart, data-driven, and approachable. We want a designer who can hold that line while the product changes quickly.

This role does not include:

  • Writing production code. Figma is your main tool, and our frontend engineers build.
  • Brand and marketing design, such as the website, sales decks, or client reports.
  • Other product surfaces like our API and MCP server.

Compensation

  • Hourly rate: $75/hour.
  • About 20 hours a week, as an independent contractor.

Recruitment Process

  2. Assessment (10 min). A quiz designed to assess your problem solving abilities and approach to work.

  4. Case study (60 min). Work through a solution to a real-world problem and record your process.

jobs.title: Data Migration and Integration Consultant (HR/Payroll Systems)
jobs.excerpt: Harbor is looking for a Data Migration and Integration Consultant to join our HR and payroll transformation practice.
jobs.description:
Harbor is looking for a Data Migration and Integration Consultant to join our HR and payroll transformation practice. This is a technical consulting role at the heart of our delivery work, responsible for moving client data safely and accurately into modern HR platforms and for designing and building the integrations that keep those platforms connected to the wider technology landscape.

You will work across engagements involving SAP SuccessFactors, Workday and Oracle HCM, taking clients from messy, fragmented legacy data through to clean, validated go live loads, and from integration requirements through to tested, supportable interfaces. The role suits someone who enjoys the detail of data work but can also explain it clearly to HR and business stakeholders who do not speak in file formats.

This is a remote position based in the UK, with travel to client sites as needed.

What you will do:

Data migration

  • Lead and deliver data migration workstreams into SAP SuccessFactors, Workday or Oracle HCM, from strategy and planning through to go live and hypercare
  • Define migration approaches, including scoping of data objects, load sequencing, cutover plans and rollback positions
  • Profile and assess legacy data quality, identifying gaps, duplicates and inconsistencies, and agreeing cleansing ownership with the client
  • Design and maintain mapping and transformation rules between legacy sources and target system structures
  • Build, execute and reconcile data loads across multiple test cycles, mock conversions and production cutover
  • Produce validation and reconciliation reporting that gives clients confidence in the accuracy and completeness of migrated data
  • Advise clients on data retention, archiving and the treatment of historical records

Integration design and delivery

  • Gather and document integration requirements across HR, payroll, benefits, finance and third party providers
  • Produce integration designs and specifications covering data flows, transformation logic, error handling, scheduling and security
  • Build, test and deploy integrations using platform native tooling and middleware
  • Support end to end and payroll parallel testing, resolving defects across connected systems
  • Define monitoring, error resolution and support processes so that integrations are sustainable after go live
  • Advise clients on integration architecture, including the trade offs between point to point connections, middleware and file based approaches

ETL and data engineering

  • Use ETL tooling to extract, transform and load data at scale across migration and integration workstreams
  • Develop repeatable, auditable transformation routines rather than one off manual manipulation
  • Automate validation and reconciliation checks where practical to reduce cycle times and manual effort
  • Contribute to the development of practice accelerators, templates and reusable migration assets

Client and practice contribution

  • Act as the trusted technical voice on engagements, translating data and integration matters into plain language for HR and programme stakeholders
  • Support proposals, scoping and estimating for migration and integration workstreams
  • Coach junior consultants and share technical knowledge across the team

What we are looking for:

Essential

  • Proven data migration experience into at least one of SAP SuccessFactors, Workday or Oracle HCM, across multiple full lifecycle projects
  • Integration design and technical delivery experience, including producing specifications and building and testing interfaces
  • Hands on experience with ETL tooling and confidence manipulating large, imperfect datasets
  • Strong understanding of HR and payroll data structures, including the sensitivities around personal data and the importance of accuracy at cutover
  • Experience running reconciliation and validation across test cycles and production loads
  • Clear communicator, able to work with both technical teams and HR stakeholders
  • Right to work in the UK and willingness to travel to client sites when needed

Desirable

  • Experience across more than one of the three target platforms
  • Knowledge of platform specific tooling such as Workday EIB, Core Connectors and Studio, SAP Integration Suite and Infoporter, or Oracle HDL and OIC
  • Experience with payroll migrations and parallel run reconciliation
  • Familiarity with UK GDPR and the data protection considerations that apply to migration and integration work
  • Exposure to professional services or legal sector clients
  • Consulting experience, or client-side experience with a clear consulting mindset

What you can expect:

  • Varied technical work across three major HR platforms, rather than being tied to a single technology
  • A collaborative practice with direct access to senior leadership and genuine input into how we grow
  • Investment in platform certifications and wider professional development
  • Competitive salary, bonus and benefits, with flexible and remote working supported

About Us:

Harbor is the preeminent provider of expert services across strategy, legal technology, operations, and intelligence. Our globally integrated team of 900+ strategists, technologists, and specialists navigate alongside our clients – leading law firms, corporations, and their law departments – to provide essential resources and invaluable insights. Anchored in a rich heritage of deep knowledge, steadfast relationships, and mutual respect, our unwavering dedication lies in shaping the future of the legal industry and fostering enduring partnerships within our community and ecosystem.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, civil union status, national origin, ancestry, age, parental status, disabled status, veteran status, or any other legally protected classification, in accordance with applicable law.
